features.title: Hydrate a per-record domain one record at a time
features.summary: Owned fork of the native storage domain form: a per-record domain whose records are disposable derived data indexes document keys at open and reads one record per table read behind a 64-row LRU, instead of materializing the whole unit into JS heap at open. The measured owner is session_projcache, whose ~2.8k checkpoints cost 252 MB of a 610 MB Host heap before this fork. Reads stay synchronous and schema-validated, writes stay durable before memory changes, and every domain that does not qualify (single layout, or per-record over authoritative records) keeps the upstream open-time loadAll.
failureModes: keys() and size count stored documents, so a document that parses as foreign stays counted until its first read drops it from the index.
A schema failure on a disposable record is backed up and skipped when first read, not at open; a domain without `invalidRecords: 'backup-and-skip'` keeps failing loud at open.
The lazy path needs the backend's synchronous per-record reads; another backend keeps the upstream loadAll path unchanged.
An empty per-record tree still calls loadAll once, because that call is the backend's legacy whole-unit bootstrap.

telemetry.reason: In-process storage reads and schema validation inside the opening consumer's existing span; no fetch, socket, or long job of its own.
